Q13 is final: drain-and-switch under the existing owner. Stop the settler and every effectful old controller, switch the center editable checkout as a complete reviewed generation, then restart. No separate principal, credential rotation, or claim that a new epoch restrains old code.

Cut over now, wave by wave after gates pass. W1 delivers M01/M02/M03/M34 independently; W2 delivers M06/M10 before any PostgreSQL migration. Each wave names center and host payloads, drains, legacy PBS/pueue settlement and rollback. v26 GH200 jobs stay queued.

Q05 is universal: every user of an owned card takes the same host-wide lease, including mainboard jobs, refactor gates and agent runs. There is no development or gate exemption. Unmanaged exclusive runs are refused.

M19/M22/M23/M24/M30/M32 and their callers now use PostgreSQL transactions, observable advisory sessions, explicit connection-loss recovery and a durable outbox across SQLAlchemy and DuckDB commits. A released advisory lock alone never proves a worker or GPU is gone.

cutover.authority: Owner decision: deploy each gated wave now via drain-and-switch under the same user. The design/implementation runs never edit the live checkout or real state. The lead performs the reviewable switch; no additional principal/credential approval question is introduced.
cutover.prepare: Prepare an immutable copy/checksum of the reviewed candidate tree and all dependency artifacts off the live path. Inventory current launchers, nested environments/.pth, processes, host runtime references, service commands and queued job envelopes. Record prior tree, config/catalog endpoint and backup. Stage everything possible before drain.
cutover.drain: Close the center admission window for controllers and prevent service auto-restart. Stop the launchd/systemd settler; wait for or stop all effectful mainboard processes, local trials that ingest/evict at close, notebooks with loaded mainboard, held keepers and their workers. Do not stop unrelated compute merely to simplify deployment. Prove each remaining process is an isolated file producer whose bytes and imports will not change. A surviving unknown writer/effect worker blocks this wave. This is operational drain by the single owner, not a security boundary against someone deliberately launching old code.
cutover.switch: While drained, replace the center editable packages/mainboard tree as a complete generation, updating outer entry points, selected nested environment metadata and service configuration in one journaled switch. A filesystem atomic rename/pointer is preferred; otherwise the drain plus checksummed journal makes an interrupted whole-tree copy non-runnable until completed or restored. Never edit live modules one by one with controllers running. Clear inherited PYTHONPATH and prove outer/nested/shell/service imports. Start one settler only after readiness and last-pass gates, then reopen admission.
cutover.hosts: Center rollout does not imply host sync. Every host receives only its wave-listed reviewed payload, staged alongside old runtime roots. Existing PATH-based queued PBS/pueue jobs retain their exact aliases/bootstrap/.pth/import roots until they drain or the delayed-start fixture proves isolation. New envelopes later use absolute immutable interpreters. A host whose shared root cannot be preserved waits; it does not cancel queued v26 GH200 work.
cutover.legacy_jobs: Every wave gate starts actual old generated PBS and pueue commands after the simulated switch, then settles their receipts through the current center. Preserve legacy target/host/handle/submitted_at identity and raw format verifiers; control migration records a deterministic SubmissionId map. Old jobs continue writing their shipped format in their run roots; new settlement can read both. Unknown finality or ambiguous identity stays pending. Never rewrite old receipts into fictitious new proof.
cutover.pause_budget: 60 s final-delta/entry-point switch budget after offline staging and successful drain, measured per wave. The owner approved the recommendation, not an unmeasured promise. If the final step cannot fit before activation, leave the old tool active and improve/rehearse staging. Drain time is visible separately and can defer a wave.
cutover.rollback: Before activation/new effects: stop/reap candidate workers and restore the recorded prior tree/config/endpoint, keeping the latest consistent legacy state. After activation: first stop admission and drain; retain new receipts/jobs and use a tested schema-compatible previous release or forward repair. Never restore a stale database over new events, never infer remote undo from local restore and never restart a pre-PostgreSQL writer against post-switch state. Unknown external effects require reconciliation. Each wave specializes this rule.

postgresql.layout: One center_id identifies one internal-disk PostgreSQL cluster. Use database mainboard, schema control and one ducklake_<canonical_LakeId> catalog schema per registered lake. control.lakes binds LakeId, metadata schema, DATA_PATH and authority; path aliases never create another owner. PGDATA defaults to <center-state>/services/postgresql/<major>/data, resolved and checked on the internal disk; socket/log/config directories are adjacent, never in a disposable environment prefix. Parquet and blob bytes stay beneath the configured external DATA_PATH. Unix socket directories must fit platform sockaddr_un limits: use a short center-ID directory in the private runtime/temp area with mode 0700 when an adjacent path is too long, and record/clean only the owned directory.
postgresql.environment: Declare conda-forge postgresql/libpq and psycopg 3 plus SQLAlchemy in workspace-owned dependency inputs. Select latest stable solvable releases at implementation, record exact locks and loaded library paths on macOS/Linux. No guessed version from current web metadata becomes a pin. Extend environment publication to retain the running server binary generation; environment upgrade cannot replace binaries under a live server. Check PG_VERSION before every start; major upgrade uses a separately rehearsed dump/restore or pg_upgrade, never automatic initdb or an unchecked new major.
postgresql.bootstrap: Mainboard owns idempotent center service prepare/start/status/stop operations. Resolve initdb/postgres/pg_ctl/pg_isready/pg_dump/pg_restore from the frozen workspace environment. On a genuinely new empty directory, run initdb -D <data> --encoding=UTF8 with an explicitly tested locale and secure local authentication. Refuse a nonempty/unrecognized directory, external/symlink-escaped PGDATA or another postmaster. Same OS owner, restrictive directory/socket permissions, loopback only where TCP is enabled; secrets use protected libpq service/pass files, never printed DSNs. These are connection hygiene, not a new principal fence.
postgresql.macos: Generate a unique center-ID LaunchAgent with absolute postgres -D arguments, explicit environment, working directory, internal log paths, KeepAlive and throttled restart. It is independent of the periodic settler agent. Prove startup/readiness under its actual service environment and retain user-login/session limitations in doctor. PostgreSQL needs no external-volume access for normal catalog service; the DuckDB worker still does, so keep checked ssh localhost for settler/replicate workers.
postgresql.linux: Generate a center-ID systemd --user service using absolute postgres -D, Type=simple, Restart=on-failure, bounded readiness/stop checks and PostgreSQL fast-shutdown semantics. Do not assume notify support in the conda build. Show whether user lingering is enabled when unattended operation requires it; no silent privileged configuration. Service-manager adapters reuse durable.py rendering/lifecycle seams without treating a server as a periodic settler pass.
postgresql.driver: Synchronous SQLAlchemy Core with explicit postgresql+psycopg dialect, psycopg 3 from the environment and libpq provenance check. Use schema-qualified SQL, short READ COMMITTED transactions with versioned conditional UPDATE and UNIQUE/CHECK/FK constraints, stable idempotency keys and RETURNING. Retry bounded SQLSTATE 40001/40P01 transactions by rereading inputs; use SERIALIZABLE only for an invariant requiring it. Pool pre-ping does not recover a lost transaction. Ownership connections are dedicated NullPool connections, never returned locked to a pool. Do not share live engines/connections across fork/spawn. Choose the environment-packaged psycopg 3 C implementation linked to its libpq when the platform solve supports it; record and gate the exact artifact instead of silently substituting psycopg2 or an untested binary wheel.
postgresql.locks: pg_try_advisory_lock on namespaced stable IDs selects one coordinator per center and one publisher per LakeId. A dedicated session can span an operation lifetime; no SQL transaction, row lock or file lock spans remote/volume I/O. pg_try_advisory_xact_lock is for short claim changes. Durable rows carry operation_id, generation, backend PID/start, local PID/start/boot, phase, deadline, heartbeat and outcome. Inspect pg_locks joined to pg_stat_activity/application_name and these rows. Configure bounded connect/statement/lock timeouts and liveness checks. PostgreSQL releases a dead session only when disconnection is detected; a stopped or partitioned client can remain visible. No lock stealing on TTL, no pg_terminate_backend without reconciliation. Never acquire a session advisory lock through DuckDB postgres_query or a pooled extension connection: ownership must remain on the dedicated psycopg session. The bounded read-only snapshot-export transaction in M38 is an explicit backup exception to short transaction lifetimes; control write transactions remain short.
postgresql.connection_loss: On lost coordinator/advisory connection or server restart, stop new effects and attempt to stop owned workers; mark surviving operations/card reservations unknown. A replacement lock owner must reconcile every prior in-flight operation and prove surviving worker incapacity before conflicting writes/releases. The durable unknown row outlives the advisory lock. If that proof is unavailable, report blocked. This is required even when only a local process crashed; an advisory lock is not a kill switch.
postgresql.transactions: The same PostgreSQL server does not make SQLAlchemy control commits and DuckDB DuckLake commits one transaction. Persist intent/outbox in control first; commit delivery/projection with a deterministic operation/event identity in one DuckLake transaction; then acknowledge in control. A crash after either commit reconciles the lake operation marker before retry. Do not use PostgreSQL user-table writes to bypass DuckLake metadata semantics, and do not invent distributed two-phase commit.
attachment_examples: ATTACH 'ducklake:postgres:dbname=mainboard host=/absolute/center/socket' AS lake (METADATA_SCHEMA 'ducklake_example', DATA_PATH '/absolute/external/data', CREATE_IF_NOT_EXISTS false, AUTOMATIC_MIGRATION false, OVERRIDE_DATA_PATH false, READ_ONLY);
ATTACH 'dbname=mainboard host=/absolute/center/socket' AS current_jobs (TYPE postgres, SCHEMA 'control', READ_ONLY);
postgresql.attachment_policy: Examples are templates for a registered existing lake. First initialization alone permits catalog creation with an explicit DATA_PATH. Writer attach omits READ_ONLY only inside M22 supervised publication. Preinstall locked ducklake/postgres extensions in the environment-owned cache; ordinary list/show must not download extensions. Existing attaches load stored DATA_PATH or compare it explicitly; override is a restore-only operation on an isolated destination. READ_ONLY plus application query restrictions prevents accidental mutations, not a hostile same-user process. Remote DuckDB clients also need access to DATA_PATH; a PostgreSQL catalog does not serve the Parquet files. Hosts do not attach the live catalog. After any catalog/schema migration, discard all DuckDB workers and native postgres schema caches and reopen fresh clients. Ownership locks stay outside duckdb-postgres connection pooling. Explicit control-query projections cannot expose arbitrary postgres_execute or connection-changing functions through a passive status query.
postgresql.status: List/show/current-status SQL are passive bounded PostgreSQL readers with observed_at, last successful pass, last attempt, owner/phase and projection watermark. No catalog migration, lake attach, service startup, host probe or reconciliation occurs as a side effect. With PostgreSQL down, return a bounded unavailable/stale response (a last-read display cache, if present, is labeled nonauthoritative). An absent external volume still permits live current-state reads when PostgreSQL is healthy. Refresh/wait explicitly enqueue targeted coordinator work and read progress.
postgresql.inlining: Set options explicitly for the exact tested extension. Initial policy: blob payload tables data_inlining_row_limit=0; narrow supported receipt/projection tables use a pilot limit of 10 rows with an application byte cap. These pilot values require M27/M38 measurement before raising them. Include null, nested JSON, strings resembling dates, unsigned extremes, decimal, timestamp and binary fixtures. No VARIANT inline assumption. Historical inline rows migrated from SQLite are retained exactly and classified; later verified flushing moves payloads to DATA_PATH.
postgresql.maintenance: Schedule explicit bounded flush/merge/rewrite operations via the same LakeId publisher, separate from lifecycle polling. Plan snapshot expiry globally against proof/reader/backup pins, and dry-run old/orphan file cleanup with a conservative age beyond every supported reader/writer/recovery window. Compaction may preserve logical history while changing physical files; raw proof retention must retain required exact bytes independently. Refuse destructive maintenance while a migration, backup, unconfirmed writer or unknown-format reachability exists. A PostgreSQL catalog removes SQLite writer contention, not external-disk stalls or file amplification.
postgresql.backup: M38 extends lake replicate: acquire a durable backup/maintenance exclusion, drain in-flight lake publication for a consistent handoff, export a REPEATABLE READ PostgreSQL snapshot, and use environment pg_dump --format=custom --snapshot=<id> --file=<staging> for the entire mainboard database. The same exported snapshot supplies control/outbox watermarks, every retained catalog file/delete-file reference and inline rows (in the dump). Keep the exporting transaction alive through dump/manifest creation; bound its lifetime. Resume append ingestion after snapshot establishment only if the fixture proves file immutability and maintenance remains blocked; otherwise remain drained. Copy and hash all referenced files, raw proofs, source/solution/runtime retention roots, configuration and a nonsecret role/bootstrap recipe. Pin copying files durably so lock/session loss cannot allow cleanup. pg_dump alone is never a successful lake replica. Publish a complete marker only after hashes and a temporary pg_restore plus DuckLake/claim readback pass. A failed copy leaves an incomplete resumable manifest and retained pins. Restore into a new cluster with effects disabled; never overlay active state. Backups provide restore-point recovery, not a promise of zero-loss PITR. Because one dump includes every registered catalog schema in the database, its completeness manifest must cover every included LakeId and DATA_PATH, or explicitly refuse a purported full-center replica. Restoring one selected lake is a separately scoped export and cannot claim to restore the whole center.
postgresql.test_harness: M00 defines a lazy postgres_cluster fixture; M36 provides its environment dependency and implementation. From an isolated test root, run environment initdb, allocate a private Unix socket and collision-safe loopback port when needed, start foreground postgres under ProcessScope and wait boundedly with pg_isready plus SQL. Supply the DSN only to the test, allow only that local endpoint through the gate, and refuse live DSNs/PGDATA. Use real fsync/durability settings for crash gates. Kill/restart fixture postmasters and clients, retain diagnostic logs, stop/reap in finalizers; no launchctl/systemctl install in integration tests. Missing binaries fail PostgreSQL-required gates explicitly; the earlier safety suite can run without requesting this fixture. Run service-rendering tests on both OSes and separately require exact-service-context rehearsal before each actual deployment. Use a short private socket directory even when pytest/report roots are long; test that cleanup does not follow a substituted socket-directory symlink.

catalog_migration: Inventory the source DuckDB build, ducklake/sqlite/postgres extension versions, DuckLake catalog spec, exact catalog schema, tables, indexes, inline data/deletes and DATA_PATH. Record source catalog content/checkpoint digest, snapshot range, next-ID counters, retained proof and all file references. Unknown spec/column/table/type blocks migration; this is a finite converter for inventoried versions.

Prepare a consistent SQLite backup with the existing SQLite backup API, including committed WAL content, under drained legacy writes. Preserve the original file read-only and every referenced data/proof byte. Bulk staging may happen earlier from a consistent checkpoint, but its final delta must come from the final drained source; no naïve mtime or latest-snapshot-only copy.

Using the same compatible locked DuckLake extension, bootstrap the PostgreSQL target catalog DDL in an isolated candidate schema/database and disposable DATA_PATH, then close every DuckDB attachment. In one exclusive import transaction replace bootstrap metadata with typed source rows, reconstruct dynamic inline tables per table/schema version, and restore all IDs/counters/snapshot validity ranges. SQLAlchemy/psycopg COPY transports data; an explicit versioned mapping validates booleans, BIGINT/unsigned bounds, decimals, timestamps/time zones, bytea and nested-text encodings. Never infer PostgreSQL types from SQLite affinity or use a blind SQLite SQL dump/pgloader default.

Preserve data_file/delete_file paths, relative-path flags, partition/schema/column mappings, view definitions, tags/options, scheduled deletion references, inline row IDs and begin/end snapshot values, encryption metadata when present, and the canonical LakeId/DATA_PATH. Do not rewrite Parquet or raw scientific receipts just to move the catalog. Reject unsupported encryption/type/features rather than drop them. Matching-spec conversion and DuckLake spec upgrade are separate gates.

Validate table counts plus typed canonical row digests and every retained snapshot/old schema read, current jobs/claim readers and blob hashes. A candidate aimed at the original DATA_PATH is read-only until activation. Write/flush/compact/expiry/restart probes use a cloned temporary DATA_PATH so old and candidate catalogs never concurrently mutate shared files.

Import legacy current job rows and raw receipt identities via M19 into control, quarantine ambiguous handles and preserve deterministic submission mappings. Reconcile the final registry/receipt delta while controllers are drained. Candidate creation is not the point of live authority: one journaled center endpoint/schema switch activates it only after M38 restore and M32 switch witnesses pass.

Before the first PostgreSQL-authority effect, rollback stops/reaps the candidate and restores the legacy endpoint/tree over untouched SQLite plus its latest checkpoint. After new effects/writes, keep PostgreSQL authoritative and forward-fix or use a tested schema-compatible previous release; never re-enable the stale SQLite writer. Keep legacy input backups and codecs until proof reachability permits retirement.

research.finding: DuckLake recommends PostgreSQL for a multi-user lakehouse with potentially remote clients.
research.design: One center PostgreSQL cluster and one mainboard database; control and ducklake_<LakeId> are separate schemas. Hosts continue to produce immutable files and receipts.

research.finding: DuckLake accepts a postgres libpq connection string, METADATA_SCHEMA and READ_ONLY. The DuckDB postgres extension also attaches native PostgreSQL schemas; these are different APIs.
research.design: Lake clients use the DuckLake attach; current job reads use SQLAlchemy directly, or a read-only postgres attachment for explicit analytical joins. Never query physical catalog tables as if they were lake tables.

research.finding: The documented DuckDB-to-DuckLake migration copies logical user data; it is not a promise to preserve an existing SQLite DuckLake catalog history. The specification describes catalog tables and backend-specific inline encodings.
research.design: Implement a bounded version-qualified metadata migration, preserving IDs, snapshot ranges, inline tables and DATA_PATH; bootstrap target DDL with the matching extension and validate before activation. This is a Mainboard design inference, not an upstream migration command.

research.finding: PostgreSQL supports inline inserts/deletes; nested values use text encoding. VARIANT cannot inline with this catalog. Flush converts inline data to Parquet while retaining snapshot semantics.
research.design: Explicitly disable inlining for blob payload tables and enable a tested small-row limit for supported narrow receipt/projection tables. Bound serialized row bytes as well as row count. Flush in supervised maintenance; never inline bulk evidence payloads onto the internal disk.

research.finding: DuckLake retries nonlogical commit conflicts without rewriting data files and aborts logical conflicts. Current configuration documents max retries 10, initial wait 100 ms and backoff 1.5; page defaults can differ by version.
research.design: Record exact versions and set retry limits explicitly within the operation deadline. Retry an entire idempotent application operation only after outcome reconciliation; never blindly repeat a submit or release.

research.finding: Merge-adjacent-files preserves time travel and does not immediately remove old files. auto_compact controls eligibility, not a background scheduler.
research.design: Keep native DuckLake compaction, with bounded file batches and before/after hash, snapshot and claim-reader tests under a PostgreSQL catalog.

research.finding: Snapshot expiry is catalog-wide; expiry and physical deletion are separate. Cleanup must account for long readers. CHECKPOINT bundles flushing, expiry, compaction and cleanup functions.
research.design: Do not run an unconditional CHECKPOINT. Select expiry candidates against retained proof, backup and read pins; use dry-run inventories and disable deletion during backup, migration or unresolved ownership.

research.finding: Session advisory locks last until unlock or session end; rollback does not release them. Transaction advisory locks end with the transaction. Advisory locks coordinate only participants and are visible in pg_locks.
research.design: Dedicated nonpooled sessions own coordinator/card/backup lifetimes. Short transaction locks protect claim changes. Join pg_locks to pg_stat_activity and Mainboard owner metadata; session loss leaves uncertain operations blocked until reconciled.

research.finding: SQLAlchemy provides the psycopg 3 sync dialect as postgresql+psycopg. Psycopg supports C, binary and Python implementations backed by libpq.
research.design: Choose synchronous SQLAlchemy Core with psycopg 3, supplied by the workspace environment with conda-forge libpq. Record the loaded implementation/library; use one SQLAlchemy pool for short connections and NullPool for ownership sessions. No ORM or second pool.

research.finding: conda-forge distributes PostgreSQL for macOS and Linux. initdb creates a cluster owned by the running user. PostgreSQL supports foreground startup under a service manager.
research.design: Resolve a stable PostgreSQL release in mainboard.toml, freeze its binary prefix, and keep PGDATA on the internal disk outside environment prefixes. Never install a system server or initialize on an external lake volume.

research.finding: launchd ProgramArguments/KeepAlive supervise a foreground process; PostgreSQL documents systemd startup, with notify support depending on the build.
research.design: Use a same-user LaunchAgent on macOS and systemd user service on Linux. Run absolute environment postgres directly; Type=simple plus a readiness probe is portable across builds. Retain the separate ssh-localhost settler path for external data access.

research.finding: pg_dump takes a consistent database snapshot and supports an exported snapshot. It is not a cluster-role or external-file backup. DuckLake documents catalog and data recovery separately and cautions about maintenance changing file layout.
research.design: lake replicate creates one custom-format dump of catalog plus control, a file/proof manifest at the same database snapshot, and verified immutable data copies while maintenance is paused. Restore in a temporary cluster before marking the replica complete.

remaining_implementation_inputs: Exact stable solvable PostgreSQL/psycopg/libpq/DuckDB/extension versions are recorded by M36 against the workspace platform matrix; current docs do not prove the carried development build matches them.

M37 inventories actual legacy catalog spec/inline schemas from a supplied read-only consistent backup. Unsupported fields or unproven time-travel conversion block only the catalog wave, not early safety releases.

Q08 still requires the named maintained palette profile and thresholds; owner acceptance of that requirement did not supply a profile. Q15 still requires the actual external NULL-Git consumer owner/predicate fixture.

Actual production service context, host legacy runtime isolation, universal card-user enrollment and measured 60 s switch remain deployment gates. No live discovery or validation was performed by this report.

global_acceptance: M00 first establishes bounded temporary execution, external-effect denial, import proof and baseline accounting. Each package adds its own golden/fault witnesses to the cumulative suite; no package waits for an unrelated fake-fleet framework. No new expected failures or unclassified skips.

Each package owns one contract or small leaf fix, plus its immediate call sites and focused scenario. No package hides a fleet rollout, data repair, whole-repository reformat, or new backend. Finish green, leave uncommitted, hand off files and one proposed commit message.

Record changed source LOC, removed implementations and dependency edges; mandatory end-state: one job reducer, one command parser, one object verification path, one process-lifetime primitive, zero implicit settlement from reads, zero target/handle-only authoritative lookups.

Use fixed checker scopes/versions established by M00. Ruff remains zero; no new pyrefly/ty/mypy or deterministic mcmr diagnostic outside an explicitly owned baseline. Fix baseline errors in changed files instead of adding ignores. Repository-wide cosmetic mcmr cleanup is excluded.

packages.title: Batch verified object access and bound materialization
changes: Extend existing Blobs.read/replication window machinery into one verified stream with deduplicated digests, byte AND row/chunk limits, ordered chunks and backpressure; no second CAS abstraction or changed chunk identity.
Fetch ordered chunks for a whole window rather than one query per ordinal/file; share verification for artifact references, restore and materialize.
Provide read-only byte estimate and explicit materialization budget before broad restore; retain exact-file/read-through use for consumers.

Use explicit pin-aware native DuckLake maintenance; never run unconditional CHECKPOINT; preserve 8 MiB chunk identity and portable archive constraints until measurements justify any separate format change.

Set options explicitly for the exact tested extension. Initial policy: blob payload tables data_inlining_row_limit=0; narrow supported receipt/projection tables use a pilot limit of 10 rows with an application byte cap. These pilot values require M27/M38 measurement before raising them. Include null, nested JSON, strings resembling dates, unsigned extremes, decimal, timestamp and binary fixtures. No VARIANT inline assumption. Historical inline rows migrated from SQLite are retained exactly and classified; later verified flushing moves payloads to DATA_PATH.

Schedule explicit bounded flush/merge/rewrite operations via the same LakeId publisher, separate from lifecycle polling. Plan snapshot expiry globally against proof/reader/backup pins, and dry-run old/orphan file cleanup with a conservative age beyond every supported reader/writer/recovery window. Compaction may preserve logical history while changing physical files; raw proof retention must retain required exact bytes independently. Refuse destructive maintenance while a migration, backup, unconfirmed writer or unknown-format reachability exists. A PostgreSQL catalog removes SQLite writer contention, not external-disk stalls or file amplification.
acceptance: Keep byte window W and row/chunk window R explicit; proposed pilot defaults W=64 MiB, R=4,096, unchanged 8 MiB chunks. Batch metadata separately, with <=R rows per batch and bounded text lengths; data buffers never exceed W plus one chunk. Stream objects larger than W across windows with incremental verification.

Fixtures cover zero-byte, many tiny, duplicate, reordered/missing chunks and multi-window objects. Let B be greedy ordered windows bounded by both W/R; assert data queries <=B, metadata queries <=ceil(unique_objects/R)+1, plus fixed measured attach setup. Count metadata and data separately; do not use a payload-only formula.

Measure cold/warm driver baseline, parent/worker/process-tree peak RSS, Python buffering, native/child file opens and bytes. Pilot fixes and checks a reference-host RSS ceiling after warmup; increasing total payload 10x at fixed W/R must not increase peak by more than proposed 32 MiB tolerance. The tolerance is a proposed gate pending measured calibration, never reported as passed by this design.

Unchanged lifecycle fixture with 1,000 settled jobs/100 streams opens or reads zero object/receipt files on the second pass, including with 32k unrelated fragments. Fail on any increase in native/child opens or queries caused by unrelated objects.

For requested-object access, require zero unrelated payload-file reads and the query-window bound above; record actual requested native file opens and a fixed corpus before/after profile. Any unavoidable catalog-metadata opens need a measured, versioned bound at the pilot before package closure.

Over-budget materialization writes zero files; within budget bytes verify and changed destinations remain protected. Real external-volume latency remains deployment-pending; the historical 447 s system-time cause is not claimed reproduced.

On temporary PostgreSQL, compare file counts, bytes, native opens and process-tree RSS before/after inline flush, merge and rewrite. Retained snapshot/claim reads match; blob payloads never silently inline, and cleanup cannot delete a pinned file.

packages.title: Make physical-card leases atomic and token-owned
changes: Replace the proposed host SQLite allocator with PostgreSQL control resource rows plus namespaced session advisory locks on canonical HostId/GPU/MIG keys. One host-wide lease-exec supervisor is used by mainboard runtime, interactive commands, refactor gates and agent runs. Its shared local root is independent of workspace; short FileLock startup/publication guards prevent competing supervisors but are not an alternative lease authority. No PostgreSQL server is installed on a compute host and hosts do not write the lake catalog.

The existing center control route mediates lease requests; no remote direct catalog credentials are shipped. Record host boot/process-start identity, request ID, purpose, all physical keys and token. Hold ownership through setup, compute descendants and cleanup, releasing only after host proof. Center communication uses bounded existing transport, not a new general message system.

Resolve masks, reordered aliases and MIG parent/child overlap before acquisition. Grant revalidation at the host verifies the current token before any compute launches. All owned-card users are enrolled; unmanaged foreign occupancy causes a visible capacity wait or exclusive-admission refusal before a scientific case.

On center/session/SSH loss the durable occupied/unknown row prevents a successor grant. Already granted compute can finish under its host supervisor and write immutable receipts; new grants fail closed until the center and host reconcile. Never reallocate on expiry or lost heartbeat alone.

Roll out a host only after legacy nonlease users drain or an exclusive scheduler boundary demonstrably isolates their cards. Queued old PBS allocations remain reserved for their scheduled computation; no gate or agent borrows them. Rollback retains the lease layer or disables new owned-card work.

200 concurrent acquire/release attempts yield zero overlaps; crash/partial-publication/stale-release witness cannot grant two owners or delete a successor.
Lease expiry while a process is alive never reallocates the card; boot-ID/process-start checks handle PID reuse.
MIG parent/child and disjoint-instance fixtures follow the declared exclusivity policy.

Use a real temporary PostgreSQL center and fake physical-card hosts: simultaneous job, gate and agent requests across three roots share one token discipline. Kill the lock backend while fake GPU children live; no successor launches. Reconnect proves token-safe release. A consumer lacking the wrapper is refused.

Pin copying files durably so lock/session loss cannot allow cleanup. pg_dump alone is never a successful lake replica. Publish a complete marker only after hashes and a temporary pg_restore plus DuckLake/claim readback pass. A failed copy leaves an incomplete resumable manifest and retained pins. Restore into a new cluster with effects disabled; never overlay active state. Backups provide restore-point recovery, not a promise of zero-loss PITR. Because one dump includes every registered catalog schema in the database, its completeness manifest must cover every included LakeId and DATA_PATH, or explicitly refuse a purported full-center replica. Restoring one selected lake is a separately scoped export and cannot claim to restore the whole center.

It contains PostgreSQL dump hash, cluster/database identity, server major/client versions, control schema version, DuckLake spec/snapshots, raw-proof/format inventory, DATA_PATH remapping, file digests, backup pins and outbox watermark. A dump is never treated as a raw PGDATA copy or a self-contained lake.

Use pg_dump and pg_restore from the retained server environment, check version compatibility, recreate the single-owner database/bootstrap role recipe and retain required extension artifacts/configuration separately. Track backup references through control rows and M03 retention so expiry/cleanup cannot race a copier after its advisory session dies. Durable incomplete backups conservatively pin required bytes until resumed or explicitly abandoned after verification.

Restore all schemas into an isolated new database/cluster, remap only destination DATA_PATH in a controlled restore, verify dump plus every file/raw object and run read-only DuckLake and JobStore/claim reads. migration.status: Wave-by-wave drain-and-switch is owner-decided now; this run supplies design only. Temporary rehearsals precede lead deployment. v26 GH200 jobs remain queued and keep their shipped code.
invariants: One active center controller generation, one PostgreSQL control authority and one publisher per canonical LakeId. Until W4 activation the legacy catalog remains sole authority; staged candidate writes are isolated.

No active editable tree is changed until its effectful mainboard processes and lazy-import consumers drain. Same-user discipline replaces the proposed principal fence; a new epoch is not an enforcement mechanism against an old binary.

Every wave preserves queued/running PBS/pueue code, old aliases and full runtime/source/environment roots. Old jobs settle through retained decoders and deterministic identity mapping; uncertain finality stays pending.

Catalog migration preserves retained snapshot and object identities. Raw evidence, historical hash algorithms and NULL-Git verified-tree proof remain intact. New logical normalization never rewrites old proof bytes.

PostgreSQL control and DuckLake transactions have separate commit boundaries. Durable outbox/operation IDs reconcile every gap; pg_dump includes both schemas and external data copying completes the checkpoint.

Locks are PostgreSQL advisory ownership sessions plus short row/transaction claims in the new architecture. An ended session or expired heartbeat does not prove a worker/card is safe; durable uncertainty blocks conflicting effects.
All owned-card compute uses the same host-wide lease, including gates and agents. A host awaiting legacy-user drain cannot grant new unmanaged shared-card work.
Each wave states rollback and measures the 60 s final switch limit; restore never undoes unknown provider/scheduler effects. After PostgreSQL activation a stale SQLite writer is never restarted.

steps.title: Inventory each wave and preserve old job runtime roots
actions: Prepare an immutable copy/checksum of the reviewed candidate tree and all dependency artifacts off the live path. Inventory current launchers, nested environments/.pth, processes, host runtime references, service commands and queued job envelopes. Record prior tree, config/catalog endpoint and backup. Stage everything possible before drain.

Center rollout does not imply host sync. Every host receives only its wave-listed reviewed payload, staged alongside old runtime roots. Existing PATH-based queued PBS/pueue jobs retain their exact aliases/bootstrap/.pth/import roots until they drain or the delayed-start fixture proves isolation. New envelopes later use absolute immutable interpreters. A host whose shared root cannot be preserved waits; it does not cancel queued v26 GH200 work.

Every wave gate starts actual old generated PBS and pueue commands after the simulated switch, then settles their receipts through the current center. Preserve legacy target/host/handle/submitted_at identity and raw format verifiers; control migration records a deterministic SubmissionId map. Old jobs continue writing their shipped format in their run roots; new settlement can read both. Unknown finality or ambiguous identity stays pending. Never rewrite old receipts into fictitious new proof.
steps.exit_gate: Concrete candidate/prior generation, process inventory, queued-job runtime map and complete backup references; unknown ownership retains data and blocks unsafe switch.

steps.title: Stage and rehearse away from the live checkout
actions: M00 defines a lazy postgres_cluster fixture; M36 provides its environment dependency and implementation. From an isolated test root, run environment initdb, allocate a private Unix socket and collision-safe loopback port when needed, start foreground postgres under ProcessScope and wait boundedly with pg_isready plus SQL. Supply the DSN only to the test, allow only that local endpoint through the gate, and refuse live DSNs/PGDATA. Use real fsync/durability settings for crash gates. Kill/restart fixture postmasters and clients, retain diagnostic logs, stop/reap in finalizers; no launchctl/systemctl install in integration tests. Missing binaries fail PostgreSQL-required gates explicitly; the earlier safety suite can run without requesting this fixture. Run service-rendering tests on both OSes and separately require exact-service-context rehearsal before each actual deployment.
Run the applicable package fault gates and delayed legacy job start/settlement fixtures. W3 stages service, W4 catalog/control conversion and complete restore; subsequent waves extend the same proof.
steps.exit_gate: Real temporary PostgreSQL where required; exact environment/extension versions and no external effects; candidate tree/environment checksums recorded.

steps.title: Drain old controllers under the existing owner
actions: Close the center admission window for controllers and prevent service auto-restart. Stop the launchd/systemd settler; wait for or stop all effectful mainboard processes, local trials that ingest/evict at close, notebooks with loaded mainboard, held keepers and their workers. Do not stop unrelated compute merely to simplify deployment. Prove each remaining process is an isolated file producer whose bytes and imports will not change. A surviving unknown writer/effect worker blocks this wave. This is operational drain by the single owner, not a security boundary against someone deliberately launching old code.
Retain runtime roots for isolated remote producers. An old held keeper or local trial that can mutate center state must finish or stop before the affected wave.
steps.exit_gate: No old effectful controller or unconfirmed worker can act through any inventoried launch route. No queued v26 job was cancelled.

steps.title: Checkpoint and apply the final delta
actions: M38 extends lake replicate: acquire a durable backup/maintenance exclusion, drain in-flight lake publication for a consistent handoff, export a REPEATABLE READ PostgreSQL snapshot, and use environment pg_dump --format=custom --snapshot=<id> --file=<staging> for the entire mainboard database. The same exported snapshot supplies control/outbox watermarks, every retained catalog file/delete-file reference and inline rows (in the dump). Keep the exporting transaction alive through dump/manifest creation; bound its lifetime. Resume append ingestion after snapshot establishment only if the fixture proves file immutability and maintenance remains blocked; otherwise remain drained. Copy and hash all referenced files, raw proofs, source/solution/runtime retention roots, configuration and a nonsecret role/bootstrap recipe. Pin copying files durably so lock/session loss cannot allow cleanup. pg_dump alone is never a successful lake replica. Publish a complete marker only after hashes and a temporary pg_restore plus DuckLake/claim readback pass. A failed copy leaves an incomplete resumable manifest and retained pins. Restore into a new cluster with effects disabled; never overlay active state. Backups provide restore-point recovery, not a promise of zero-loss PITR.
Before W4 use a consistent SQLite input backup and M37 final-delta validation; after W4 use M38 PostgreSQL plus external-data checkpoints. Do not run two active catalogs against the same DATA_PATH.
steps.exit_gate: Restorable complete checkpoint and final identity/catalog/control watermarks within the measured switch budget; otherwise keep prior authority active.

steps.title: Switch the complete center editable generation and selected host payloads
actions: While drained, replace the center editable packages/mainboard tree as a complete generation, updating outer entry points, selected nested environment metadata and service configuration in one journaled switch. A filesystem atomic rename/pointer is preferred; otherwise the drain plus checksummed journal makes an interrupted whole-tree copy non-runnable until completed or restored. Never edit live modules one by one with controllers running. Clear inherited PYTHONPATH and prove outer/nested/shell/service imports. Start one settler only after readiness and last-pass gates, then reopen admission.

60 s final-delta/entry-point switch budget after offline staging and successful drain, measured per wave. The owner approved the recommendation, not an unmeasured promise. If the final step cannot fit before activation, leave the old tool active and improve/rehearse staging. Drain time is visible separately and can defer a wave.
Hosts follow their own wave live_switch entry; preserve old aliases/import roots and defer unisolatable host changes.
steps.exit_gate: Outer/nested/shell/service import proof and one current controller; PostgreSQL/database/volume freshness health reflects actual context.

steps.title: Settle late old jobs and observe the new wave
actions: Every wave gate starts actual old generated PBS and pueue commands after the simulated switch, then settles their receipts through the current center. Preserve legacy target/host/handle/submitted_at identity and raw format verifiers; control migration records a deterministic SubmissionId map. Old jobs continue writing their shipped format in their run roots; new settlement can read both. Unknown finality or ambiguous identity stays pending. Never rewrite old receipts into fictitious new proof.

Verify new submissions use the negotiated current decoder/runtime, late old receipts settle once, status is passive after W4, and universal card consumers all use the same lease after host enrollment.

steps.title: Retire only unreachable executable generations
actions: Review queued/running/held jobs, raw evidence readers, checkpoints and pending effects before deletion. Preserve all historical verifier codecs and exact referenced source/solution/data bytes.
Repeat the common switch for any executable removal. Unknown reachability retains the generation and prevents destructive cleanup.

rollback.before_new_writes: Before activation/new effects: stop/reap candidate workers and restore the recorded prior tree/config/endpoint, keeping the latest consistent legacy state. After activation: first stop admission and drain; retain new receipts/jobs and use a tested schema-compatible previous release or forward repair. Never restore a stale database over new events, never infer remote undo from local restore and never restart a pre-PostgreSQL writer against post-switch state. Unknown external effects require reconciliation. Each wave specializes this rule.
rollback.after_new_writes: Pause admission and drain; preserve current PostgreSQL catalog/control and newly arrived receipts. Roll back code only to a tested schema/envelope-compatible release; otherwise checkpoint and forward-repair. Reverse migration to SQLite is not supplied or assumed.
rollback.external_effects: Submissions/cancels/provider release are not undone by restore. Reconcile stable tokens/receipts, retaining unknown effects. Running and queued jobs keep their runtimes/output roots.
rollback.lake_format: Catalog-engine migration, DuckLake specification upgrades and application table changes are distinct. M37 preserves the inventoried supported catalog spec. An engine/spec change needs its own retained-snapshot/readback/restore gate and cannot be hidden in W4.
rollback.per_wave: Every order.waves entry contains a concrete rollback and center/host/drain/legacy switch. Common protocol is in decisions.cutover.

open_questions.decision: Where should mutable job state live?
open_questions.recommended_answer: One center_id identifies one internal-disk PostgreSQL cluster. Use database mainboard, schema control and one ducklake_<canonical_LakeId> catalog schema per registered lake. control.lakes binds LakeId, metadata schema, DATA_PATH and authority; path aliases never create another owner. PGDATA defaults to <center-state>/services/postgresql/<major>/data, resolved and checked on the internal disk; socket/log/config directories are adjacent, never in a disposable environment prefix. Parquet and blob bytes stay beneath the configured external DATA_PATH. Unix socket directories must fit platform sockaddr_un limits: use a short center-ID directory in the private runtime/temp area with mode 0700 when an adjacent path is too long, and record/clean only the owned directory.
open_questions.reason: The owner selected a shared PostgreSQL catalog/control server; this supersedes the v2 SQLite recommendation.

open_questions.decision: Should job list/show/query remain implicit settlement commands?
open_questions.recommended_answer: List/show/current-status SQL are passive bounded PostgreSQL readers with observed_at, last successful pass, last attempt, owner/phase and projection watermark. No catalog migration, lake attach, service startup, host probe or reconciliation occurs as a side effect. With PostgreSQL down, return a bounded unavailable/stale response (a last-read display cache, if present, is labeled nonauthoritative). An absent external volume still permits live current-state reads when PostgreSQL is healthy. Refresh/wait explicitly enqueue targeted coordinator work and read progress.
open_questions.reason: PostgreSQL provides current control reads independently of the external lake data volume; listing never becomes an effect executor.

open_questions.recommended_answer: One sealed SourceSnapshot for all capture origins, plus an immutable detached approval selected by acquisition. Bind full first-party bundle, exact EnvironmentSolution and input identities; never update approval during capture/submit. Use existing registration entry points, with owner-explicit creation.
open_questions.reason: A target commit alone does not freeze the tool or dependent editable imports. The owner retained design-v2; this report does not create or select an actual acquisition approval.

open_questions.decision: What is the default for already-complete registered cases?
open_questions.recommended_answer: A registered acquisition creates a new attempt by default. Reuse must be explicit and produce a local reuse receipt with counts; never submit a zero-work remote pytest job. Preserve consumer-specific freshness flags only inside their owned argv.
open_questions.reason: Silent all-skipped execution is neither a fresh acquisition nor a useful dispatched job.

open_questions.decision: How strong must the shared-GPU guarantee be?
open_questions.recommended_answer: Q05 is universal: every user of an owned card takes the same host-wide lease, including mainboard jobs, refactor gates and agent runs. There is no development or gate exemption. Unmanaged exclusive runs are refused.
open_questions.reason: The owner requires every owned-card user, including agents and gates, to enroll. Strong exclusive admission also verifies the managed boundary; unmanaged occupancy is not a trial failure.

open_questions.decision: May a spend cap release a rental before required evidence arrives?
open_questions.recommended_answer: Stop compute at the cap and reserve collection headroom in the admission budget. If the hard financial cap forces release, record evidence_lost and the explicit cap policy; do not certify or silently reuse evidence.
open_questions.reason: Unlimited retention and a hard spend limit cannot both be guaranteed during a permanent evidence outage.

open_questions.decision: How should local restore conflicts behave?
open_questions.recommended_answer: Refuse overwrite by default and list expected/current digests. A separately explicit replace command first preserves the edited bytes as a recoverable object and records the disposition.
open_questions.reason: A logical lake path does not grant permission to erase a newer result.

open_questions.decision: Which palette metrics and thresholds are house policy?
open_questions.recommended_answer: Before M09, select and version a named existing or maintained validator profile and its numerical thresholds. Require contrast, lightness order, chroma bounds, perceptual separation and requested CVD fixtures; unavailable metrics keep B46 open. Do not invent thresholds or count unsupported as success.
open_questions.reason: No cited profile/threshold set has been verified by this revision; this decision gates M09 only.

open_questions.decision: Keep the macOS ssh-localhost service access path?
open_questions.recommended_answer: Keep it initially, with exact-context access checks and complete-pass supervision. Replace it only after an alternative launch identity proves access to the external volume in a manual rollout rehearsal.
open_questions.reason: The local code fix does not prove launchd has Full Disk Access; Python cannot grant that permission.

open_questions.decision: How much cutover interruption is acceptable?
open_questions.recommended_answer: Use a measured 60 s maximum final-delta/switch write pause after staging and safe drain, per wave. Isolated file producers continue; unsafe drain defers a wave/host. Abort before activation on overrun; after new effects retain current state and forward-recover.
open_questions.reason: Zero pause with two unfenced legacy/new writers cannot provide the intended ownership guarantees.

open_questions.decision: Which historical runs and fleet entries should be retained or retired?
open_questions.recommended_answer: Inventory first; retain raw evidence and unresolved runs until explicitly dispositioned. Route the self host locally, decide pedro-home separately, and recheck site maintenance/queue facts during rollout.
open_questions.reason: The audit cannot decide scientific retirement, ownership of fleet entries or current site schedules.

open_questions.decision: Should objects move out of DuckLake in this campaign?
open_questions.recommended_answer: No. Batch reads, normalize receipts and separate control-state access first. Reconsider a packed store only if the M27 profile still identifies object-file layout as the limiting cost and a publication/backup/GC pilot passes.
open_questions.reason: A store replacement creates a new two-resource commit problem and is not required to remove the proven replay and per-object-query defects.

open_questions.decision: How will unmodified legacy controllers lose effect authority?
open_questions.recommended_answer: Q13 is final: drain-and-switch under the existing owner. Stop the settler and every effectful old controller, switch the center editable checkout as a complete reviewed generation, then restart. No separate principal, credential rotation, or claim that a new epoch restrains old code.
open_questions.reason: The owner controls center and hosts under one user. Old controllers are stopped operationally; no new epoch/advisory lock is claimed to restrain an unmodified legacy process.

open_questions.decision: How should incompatible native collection or solve-only forms behave?
open_questions.recommended_answer: Refuse with the missing capability before acquisition effects; use a supported compatible prepare/tool environment only after its exact native behavior is verified. Do not rebuild pytest grammar or a registry-based compatibility solver.
open_questions.reason: Target-platform collection and native lock support cannot be inferred from a successful center-only test.

open_questions.decision: Who closes the NULL-Git admission incident?
open_questions.recommended_answer: Assign the owner of the actual failing consumer and obtain its receipt/predicate fixture. Keep that portion E05 consumer/deployment-pending until its real read path admits verified non-Git proof.
open_questions.reason: Current mainboard paths already accept digest/closure proof; changing a codec alone cannot prove the reported downstream rejection is fixed.

findings.title: Dependency reuse must name concrete implementation choices
findings.reason: Use DuckDB extract_statements/get_table_names, PyYAML syntax and native solving; refuse unsupported solver forms instead of reconstructing a solver.

findings.title: Three migration layers are unnecessary
findings.reason: Use one center orchestrator and checkpoint manifest. M37 supplies the versioned catalog converter; M38 supplies pg_dump plus referenced data backup; SQLite backup remains a legacy input primitive.

findings.title: Typing rules are absent from acceptance
findings.reason: Require house immutable models and changed-boundary Any/object/suppression audits; apply model policy at these seams without an unrelated repository-wide dataclass rewrite.

findings.title: Object I/O bounds omit metadata and have no measured baseline
findings.reason: Use byte/row/chunk windows on existing Blobs, keep zero idle reads unconditional and treat RSS/throughput tolerances as pilot gates pending measurement.

findings.title: The initial harness risks becoming a blocking framework
findings.reason: M00 first proves isolation/baseline; each owning package grows existing fixtures and cumulative golden/fault coverage.

findings.title: Legacy queued scripts do not pin their runtime
findings.reason: Pin new scripts by absolute versioned runtime and preserve old PATH aliases/editables until actual delayed-start, child-import and held-keeper fixtures pass.

findings.title: New epochs cannot fence unmodified legacy writers
findings.reason: Owner supersedes the proposed principal fence with a tested process drain and complete editable-tree switch. A surviving old controller blocks handoff; same-user old-code denial is not claimed.

findings.title: Center launcher switching misses nested environments
findings.reason: Include Provisioner readers, all selected workspace generations, shells/tasks/.pth and outer/nested/service import proofs without the audit guard.

findings.title: Ordinary scheduler acceptance has an unrecorded-effect window
findings.reason: Track C-SUBMIT-ACK and commit plan/pins/token/intent before every backend; lost replies reconcile or remain unknown without resubmission.

findings.title: Quota-held requests mutate and collide
findings.reason: Track C-HELD-PLAN and retain a distinct SubmissionId plus sealed resolved plan across retry; legacy unresolved holds require explicit preparation.

findings.title: Remote logs and exit records alias reused scheduler IDs
findings.reason: Track C-REMOTE-ATTEMPT and carry identity through runtime, script, logs, sampler/framing and scheduler/autopsy APIs before status closure.

findings.title: Per-run output roots still relink a shared snapshot
findings.reason: Give each SubmissionId an immutable execution directory/mount table and convert agent/dispatcher/claim-path readers; test overlapping identical bundles.

findings.title: Collect-only cannot decide scientific reuse/fresh policy
findings.reason: Separate syntax/collection from trial admission using target axes/facts, input identities and watermark, then enforce that selection at runtime.

findings.title: Registered acquisition needs an independent approval authority
findings.reason: Define detached immutable approval binding acquisition/source/solution/inputs, with explicit selection and positive and mismatch tests across all entry paths.

findings.title: NULL-Git incident and parity are not proven by a codec change
findings.reason: Keep the actual rejecting consumer externally pending and compare common-schema/claim-reader output with row-specific expected corrections.

findings.title: Historical formats/verifiers need a concrete inventory
findings.reason: Record each raw format and exact verifier family, keep legacy identities beside projections, and test restore/late/compacted/unknown cases.

findings.title: Supervised I/O conflicts with live connection and callback APIs
findings.reason: Convert all connection-escaping callers after M35, execute/consume operations inside fresh workers and test hangs through commit/close.

findings.title: Writer authority must follow LakeId and cover served access
findings.reason: Bind canonical LakeId to one control authority, route or refuse other workspaces and disable unsupported served writes including write=False escalation.

findings.title: Verified lake custody does not prevent local replacement loss
findings.reason: Track C-EVICT-RACE and require finalized/coordinated output with exact-candidate quarantine; never unlink a changed successor or race an uncoordinated writer.

findings.title: Walltime misses pre-command helpers
findings.reason: Track C-PREP-DEADLINE and propagate one budget plus reserved cleanup grace through provision/activate/attest/wait/command; retain child and GPU ownership.

findings.title: Delivery needs producer finality, including legacy fragments
findings.reason: Bind closed manifest to termination, support incomplete-but-final failures and retain legacy evidence pending stable inventory proof.

findings.title: Several acceptance criteria are vacuous or underdefined
findings.reason: Specify query classes, semantic reducer comparisons, dual I/O limits, measured profiles, minimum palette support and explicit pause/parity gates.

findings.title: B map alone omits requested closure obligations
findings.reason: Keep B IDs stable and add an issue-level ledger for all original issues, five source-traced defects, resource inclusion and the pending NULL consumer.

findings.title: Coverage is aligned only after missing paths are owned
findings.reason: Retain all 36 primary package mappings and incorporate the table's call sites, prerequisites and conditional closure; M33 cannot absorb missing behavior.

acceptance_subfindings.reason: Status/constant queries have zero lake I/O; requested evidence queries are bounded/read-only and cannot create/evolve state.
Compare normalized semantics under authority/sequence/conflict rules rather than incidental versions and arrival timestamps.
Replace the guessed payload-only formula with byte/row windows and separately counted metadata/data batches plus measured process-tree RSS.
Zero idle object/file reads and no unrelated payload access are pass/fail gates; native file-open baselines must be measured before closure.
A versioned threshold/reference profile and minimum supported metrics gate M09; unsupported requested checks keep B46 open.
Specify reference host/sample/percentile for transaction targets and recommend a rehearsed 60 s final handoff budget without claiming measurements.
Compare explicit common columns with fixture-row-specific expected deltas and verify claim-reader paths.
